tweets.text:
Last night, we witnessed a devastating tragedy in New York City, as the Mexican Navy ship Cuauhtemoc allided with the Brooklyn Bridge. The Coast Guard extends our condolences to the crew of Cuauhtemoc and the families of those impacted by this accident.

Following the allision, the Coast Guard immediately responded, launching a crew from Station New York and establishing a temporary safety zone. We are grateful for the timely, diligent efforts by our federal, state, and local partners in coordinating that initial response. As the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) begins its investigation, the Coast Guard will provide full support, while maintaining the safety and security of the Port of New York.

The Coast Guard will continue to ensure fulsome assistance for those impacted, and provide updates as appropriate in coordination with our interagency partners.

@USCGNortheast

tweets.text:
The U.S. Coast Guard plays a crucial role in securing the nations Maritime Domain and Marine Transportation System by strengthening cyber security!

Coast Guard Cyber Command (CGCYBER) recently published the 2024 Cyber Trends and Insights in the Marine Environment (CTIME) Report that provides thought provoking analysis and trends for the maritime cyber community, and in-depth discussions regarding ship-to-shore cranes manufactured in China, cyber risks to vessels, and analysis of cloud infrastructure in the marine environment.

Read more here: https://t.co/GUzK9AG9kp

tweets.text:
The USCGC STRATTON WMSL-752 has deployed and been assigned to Destroyer Squadron 15, the largest surface force in the U.S. 7th Fleet! 

With over 150 years of U.S. Coast Guard operations in the vital Indo-Pacific Region, the we are ramping up our efforts to enhance maritime security and national defense for ourselves and our allied nations.

Through strategic patrols with ​national security cutters, fast response cutters, and collaborative activities, the we are committed to strengthening our regional partnerships and ensuring safe, secure waters for all.

The USCGC Stratton is a 418-foot Legend-class national security cutter, homeported in Alameda, California.

📷: Petty Officer 3rd Class William Kirk
